source: src/live.md (old Notion page 'Profiling and tools', fetched 2026-09-22, saved by the parent as read/old/05_profiling.md)

claims.claim: Nsight Compute docs (~2h) and Nsight Systems docs (~1h); Kernel Profiling Guide worth reading end to end
claims.verdict: carried
claims.where: Further reading (Profiling Guide 2 h, CLI, Nsight Systems User Guide 1 h)

claims.claim: GPU MODE lecture 1 (profiling PyTorch) and lecture 8 (CUDA performance checklist)
claims.verdict: verified (github.com/gpu-mode/lectures: titles and speaker)

claims.claim: PyTorch profiler recipe (25 min) and Holistic Trace Analysis
claims.verdict: verified (HTA README)

claims.claim: CUDA C++ Best Practices Guide, performance metrics (timing with events, effective bandwidth)
claims.verdict: carried

claims.claim: Microbenchmark papers (dissecting lineage) for ground-truth latencies
claims.verdict: carried as Luo et al. 2402.13499 (FACTS.md)

claims.claim: nsys: whole-program timeline of CPU threads, CUDA API, kernels, memcpies, NCCL, NVTX; answers where wall-clock time goes; start here; cheap
claims.verdict: verified (Nsight Systems User Guide v2026.5; Profiling Guide: no clock locking, single pass); 'non-perturbing' softened to 'low cost'

claims.claim: nsys profile -o out python train.py; torch.cuda.nvtx.range_push/pop
claims.verdict: verified (torch.cuda.nvtx functions in 2.14.1; --trace defaults cuda,opengl,nvtx,osrt); capture range and nsys stats report names added

claims.claim: ncu: per-kernel microscope, replays each kernel many times, heavily perturbing; use on convicted kernels
claims.verdict: verified and measured: NVIDIA's reports needed 42 passes and saved/restored 545 MB per pass (transpose)

claims.claim: ncu --set full -k regex:my_kernel -c 10 -o out python ...
claims.verdict: verified flags from ncu --help 2026.3.1 (page uses -c 1)

claims.claim: torch.profiler built on CUPTI; per-op CPU+GPU time, stacks, Chrome/Perfetto export, memory timelines; schedule with warmup; with_stack sparingly
claims.verdict: verified (Kineto README and CuptiActivityApi sources); run here on CPU and MPS

claims.claim: CUPTI is the library these tools sit on; usable directly for custom telemetry
claims.verdict: carried (definition)

claims.claim: compute-sanitizer memcheck/racecheck; run before trusting a new kernel; cuda-gdb; nvidia-smi dmon / nvitop
claims.verdict: verified (compute-sanitizer --help: four tools; cuda-gdb in the toolkit; dmon in nvidia-smi docs); nvitop named as third-party

claims.claim: Speed of Light first: SM % and Memory %; regimes memory-bound / compute-bound / latency
claims.verdict: verified (Profiling Guide definition) and shown on NVIDIA's reports

claims.claim: Achieved occupancy sm__warps_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_active, grid vs SM count, waves per SM
claims.verdict: verified by ncu --query-metrics on ga100/gh100/gb100/gb202; launch__waves_per_multiprocessor is a launch attribute

claims.claim: Occupancy limiters: registers, smem/block, block size
claims.verdict: carried; occupancy rules owned by programming_model

claims.claim: HBM saturated: dram__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed vs ~1.79 TB/s on a 5090
claims.verdict: verified (metric exists on all four chips; SOL label uses gpu__dram_throughput; 1,792 GB/s from FACTS.md)

claims.claim: Coalescing: L1/TEX sectors per request (~4 ideal for 32-bit)
claims.verdict: verified; shown measured on NVIDIA's uncoalesced pair (24 vs 8 for 8-byte)

claims.claim: Bank conflicts: l1tex__data_bank_conflicts_pipe_lsu_mem_shared_op_ld/st
claims.verdict: verified (all four chips); measured 96.4% of wavefronts in NVIDIA's transpose

claims.claim: Divergence: branch efficiency, smsp__thread_inst_executed_per_inst_executed (32 = none)
claims.verdict: verified

claims.claim: SMs busy: sm__cycles_active vs elapsed; tail effect
claims.verdict: verified metric

claims.claim: Tensor cores used: sm__pipe_tensor_cycles_active, HMMA/QMMA in the instruction mix
claims.verdict: verified metric on all four chips

claims.claim: Spills: local memory traffic in MWA; confirm with ptxas -v
claims.verdict: verified (l1tex__t_requests_pipe_lsu_mem_local_op_ld)

claims.claim: Guided analysis rules engine: trust as hypothesis generator, verify with counters
claims.verdict: confirmed with NVIDIA's data: estimated 64.67%, measured 0.14%; estimated 87.21%, measured 29.7%

claims.claim: ncu locks clocks to base by default (--clock-control base)
claims.verdict: CORRECTED: default boost since Nsight Compute 2026.1 (release notes; --help shows =boost); base was the default until 2025.x, visible in NVIDIA's 2023 reports (about 1 GHz vs 1.65 GHz max)

claims.claim: Async: host timers lie; synchronize; cudaEvent pattern; events exclude host overhead; host timer+sync to include launch overhead
claims.verdict: verified (CUDA Runtime API, 0.5 us resolution) and measured on M1 (0.18 vs 4.24 vs 4.15 ms; 19.9 ms with queued work)

claims.claim: Warmup 3-10+ runs; torch.compile compiles per shape; median or trimmed mean, not min, not a single run
claims.verdict: measured (first-call costs, three-run spread)

claims.claim: Lock clocks: nvidia-smi -lgc, -lmc, -pl; unlock -rgc; dual-5090 workstation fans/power/ambient
claims.verdict: verified (nvidia-smi docs; -lmc not on Hopper, use deferred); workstation advice generalised (no GPU here)

claims.claim: Beware the cache: rotate buffers larger than L2 (96 MB on a 5090) or flush
claims.verdict: verified and measured (16 MB hot 1.7x faster than cold on M1)

claims.claim: do_bench has flush_l2=True, does warmup and median
claims.verdict: CORRECTED: no flush_l2 argument in Triton 3.8.0; it always zeroes a 256 MB buffer; returns the mean by default

claims.claim: Fair baselines: torch.compile not eager, cuBLAS with right epilogue/dtype/layouts; check outputs first; report achieved GB/s or TFLOPs vs roofline
claims.verdict: carried

claims.claim: CUDA graphs / launch overhead: measure graphed and ungraphed for microsecond kernels
claims.verdict: carried; measured launch-bound regime on M1 (5 us batched vs 0.196 ms per synchronised call); do_bench_cudagraph

claims.claim: Environment log: GPU, driver, CUDA/toolkit (13.3 current), PyTorch/Triton, clocks
claims.verdict: CORRECTED version: CUDA 13.4.2 current (FACTS.md)

claims.claim: AMD Hyperloom shipped in ROCm.AI Aug 2026; profiles, analyses, plans and validates; weeks to hours (AMD claim)
claims.verdict: verified (ROCm blog Aug 27 2026; inference workload optimisation)

claims.claim: Dream-RSI (Sep 2026): replay-simulator method, GPU kernel engineering among three domains, competitive or better quality at lower discovery cost
claims.verdict: verified (arXiv 2609.14858, Sep 14 2026)

claims.claim: Phi-Bench: Hardware and Edge worst category at 5.4%
claims.verdict: unconfirmed (no arXiv result); dropped with a note

claims.claim: The gap closes through cheaper search and vendor packaging, not better models
claims.verdict: opinion; not carried (unsourced)

claims.claim: An agent reporting a speedup without locked clocks, warmup and L2 flush has reported nothing
claims.verdict: carried

claims.claim: Workflow: nsys -> top kernels/gaps -> torch.profiler -> ncu full on guilty kernel -> roofline hypothesis -> change one thing -> re-measure with locked clocks and do_bench; write numbers down; Boehm worklog
claims.verdict: carried
